text: Heikki Aittokumpu – Technical and AI Development Expertise

Heikki Aittokumpu is a versatile software and AI developer with broad experience in modern machine learning, data management, and software engineering. He has strong practical skills in Python, Android development, deep learning, and building AI-based applications.

Heikki has implemented several applied AI projects, including a name generator using RNNs, a Finnish–English translator based on GRU networks, and a material classification system for culvert pipes using ResNet50 and EfficientNet models. He has designed segmentation pipelines that employ the Segment Anything Model (SAM) for object detection and masking prior to classification. His projects include step-by-step testing in Jupyter notebooks, model training with PyTorch, and structured storage of model metadata, hyperparameters, and results in a MariaDB database.

Heikki also has deep knowledge of databases and data workflows. He has built Docker-based systems that store image paths, embeddings, and model metadata, and he has used FiftyOne, DuckDB, and MariaDB for AI data pipelines. He has designed vector-database-based retrieval systems and integrated them into RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) architectures.

In software engineering, Heikki is proficient with Git, GitHub, and GitLab for version control, including branch management and repository migration. He also works with containerization tools such as Docker and Docker Swarm. He has developed web-based AI tools (using Streamlit and React) that combine document editing, proofreading, technical rewriting, translation, and subscription-based user interfaces.

His strengths also include data analysis and signal processing, using moving averages and histograms to study measurement accuracy and performance in tuning and averaging applications. He applies experimental and statistical approaches to evaluate model learning and smoothing effects.

Heikki has also developed language-model-powered systems that scrape and process website content (for example, kamk.fi), store the results in DuckDB, generate embeddings, and use them for retrieval-augmented language model responses. He understands the full structure and implementation of RAG architectures.

Heikki’s working style is experimental, iterative, and grounded in the scientific method. He documents his projects thoroughly, tests multiple neural architectures in parallel, and optimizes for accuracy and performance. His core interests lie in the use of neural networks for visual recognition, intelligent search systems, and adaptive user interfaces.
